[DataSquad logged {{< var datasquad.tasks_2025 >}} reportable project tasks in 2025.]{.lede}

DataSquad is DSC's peer-consulting model: undergraduate and graduate student
consultants providing sustained project support alongside DSC staff's direct
consultations. Much of its work is sustained, hands-on project support rather than one-off
questions. Task
tracking in Trello began in 2023, so the rise from {{< var datasquad.tasks_2023 >}} tasks
that year partly reflects record-keeping, not only more work.

The program started in 2020 on a gift from **Norman Powell**, which funded student
salaries and laptops for the first cohort, and became a formal program in 2021. The Library added funding in 2023 to
expand the team and add in-person hours. In 2024, DataSquad absorbed the LuxLab
student program after its funding source, CLICC funds, became restricted, merging two
student-support lines into one.

It also prepares students for data careers. DSC documented post-graduation destinations for
{{< var datasquad.placement_n >}} DataSquad graduates from {{< var datasquad.placement_cohort >}}, and all
of them found placements, at employers including {{< var datasquad.placement_names >}}. That is
a tracked group, not an outcome rate for every student in the program. Several of the same students worked
on DataSquad's highest-profile faculty projects before landing those placements.
Lawrence Lee, who built the codebooks the BioCritical Studies Lab uses to update its
dataset, is now a Software Development Engineer at Amazon.
